transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-05-12 11:00 AM PT / 2:00 PM ET
Duration: ~46 minutes
Recording ID: ff-record-8432
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM); Michael Turner (Aurora CTO), Jasmine Patel (Lead ML Eng), Eli Moreno (DevOps), Sandra Ruiz (Procurement)

Summary:
- Walkthrough of Redwood Console per-route dashboards, token & cost breakdown, and Optimize suggestions for cost/perf.
- Customer is evaluating trade-offs between Hosted vs Dedicated for patient-facing summarization and embeddings.
- Next steps: share billing export + pilot config, SOC 2 docs, schedule pilot.

Topics covered (auto): console dashboards, per-route cost, token-level breakdowns, caching/batching recommendations, Dedicated pilots, security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time — we'll run about 45 minutes — quick intro from our side. i'm alex, i'll lead the demo and priya will jump into the console and runtime bits.
[00:20] Michael (Aurora): thanks alex, i'm michael, i'll be the CS lead on this evaluation, jasmine and eli are on to cover ML infra and ops, and sandra is here for procurement notes.
[00:36] Priya (Redwood SE): hi all, priya here — i'll share my screen in a sec and walk through the per-route dashboards — just a heads up the tenant i set up is seeded with three sample routes: /chat, /summaries, and /embed-v1.
[01:02] Jasmine (Aurora): perfect, our main concern is cost variability — we saw token spikes last month and want to understand the console's breakdown so we can budget.
[01:18] Alex: absolutely — that's what we'll focus on, plus optimize suggestions (batching, kv cache, quant profiles). note: some of the auto captions might say "optima" instead of Optimize, ignore that haha.

[02:05] [Screen share starts — Redwood Console visible]
[02:12] Priya: okay pulling up the "Routes" overview — top left is global usage time-series, center shows per-route TPS and p50/p95 latency, right side is cost breakdown by route and model variant. we also have a token-level table which maps tokens to cost buckets — this is the per-token cost, amortized across batched requests.
[02:45] Eli (Aurora): wait — is that cost showing tokenized input + generated tokens or just generations?
[02:50] Priya: good question — it's both, the breakdown has columns for prompt_tokens and completion_tokens and a cost_per_1k_tokens derived from the model profile. sometimes the transcription will say "prompts and completions" weirdly as prompt-complete, but that's the idea.
[03:18] Michael: can we filter by route, model version, and customer tag? we tag requests by tenant and dataset.
[03:25] Priya: yes — top filter bar supports route, model, env (prod/staging), and any custom tags you push in headers. we even let you pivot by customer_id for multi-tenant orgs.

[04:10] [00:04:10] Priya: diving into /summaries route — you can see steady state at ~12 req/s, p95 latency 240ms when running hosted small model, cost center shows $0.024 per 1k tokens at current profile. the route panel also highlights anomalies — last week we had a 2-hour spike due to a bad prompt loop and it surfaces the likely root cause with sample request traces.
[04:42] Jasmine: sample traces — does that include the raw prompt text? we need to keep PHI out of logs.
[04:51] Priya: those traces are redacted by default — the console shows token-level delta and shape but you can toggle to see full text if you have the right role and if the tenant is configured to retain raw text. for PHI workloads we recommend disabling raw text retention and using hashed IDs; that is also in the network/compliance docs.
[05:20] Sandra (Procurement): what's the retention window? 90 days is what we typically ask for.
[05:25] Marcus (Redwood CSM): default is 30 days for hosted analytics, but for enterprise plans you can pay for extended retention (90/365) or push logs to your S3/logging pipeline via the audit export feature.

[06:00] [00:06:00] Priya: switching to the cost drill — here's the per-route cost waterfall, it breaks down compute (GPU), model variant premium (if you're using a larger variant), and infra overhead like network egress. the console attributes cost to requests using sampling and deterministic attribution so you can see both absolute dollars and percent of total.
[06:27] Michael: how accurate is the attribution? we need to reconcile with our own chargeback reports.
[06:33] Priya: accurate within noise — we provide a billing export CSV with per-request attribution you can import into your chargeback system. the sampling is conservative; when you enable dedicated mode the attribution becomes exact because we map capacity to route pins.
[07:00] Jasmine: speaking of dedicated — if we move /summaries to Dedicated GPUs, how does the console show opportunity cost savings?
[07:08] Priya: good one — we have a "What-if" overlay: switch a route to Dedicated and the console simulates cost trajectories using your traffic patterns; it recommends instance sizes and shows projected $/1M tokens. it also flags break-even points — for your traffic pattern i expect Dedicated to be attractive if p95 load stays above ~30 req/s sustained.

[08:12] [00:08:12] Alex: there's also Optimize suggestions — on the same panel you'll see recommended batching windows, cacheable prefixes for the summary route (we detected 12% prefix reuse), and quantization profiles for embeddings that could save 35% on compute. the suggestion sometimes appears as "redwood optima" in transcripts but it's Optimize.
[08:40] Eli: prefix reuse — is that head caching / KV cache or something else?
[08:45] Priya: it's the KV cache / prefix cache — we surface which prompt prefixes are repeated and how much tokens you'd save with a small cache hit rate. you can toggle to auto-insert a prefix cache policy on a route and test it in canary.

[09:25] Jasmine: are these recommendations automatically applied or manual?
[09:28] Priya: they're suggestions — you can apply them with one click to a canary rollout (e.g., 5% traffic), monitor quality metrics, and then roll out gradually. we log the eval results against your baseline prompt sets.

[10:12] [00:10:12] Priya: next i'll show the per-model variant cost comparison table — it lists available variants, tokens/sec, expected latency at your seq lengths, and estimated cost per 1k tokens. this is where you can choose a cheaper LLM variant for low-stakes endpoints.
[10:42] Michael: can we set SLO based routing? like route /chat should prefer low-latency variants and fallback to cheaper ones when under load.
[10:49] Alex: yes — smart routing policies allow you to declare SLOs per route and set priorities: prefer low-latency variants, fallback to cost-saving variants, or redirect to a cached precomputed response. the console exposes these settings with a simulated load test.

[11:30] [00:11:30] Jasmine: about cost breakdown — is tokenization consistent across different models? we use long-context summarization and token counting differences matter.
[11:40] Priya: tokenization differences are considered. the model profile includes tokenizer mapping and the console normalizes cost to the active tokenizer so you can compare apples-to-apples. there's a note that sometimes transcriptions mistakenly say "tokenizer map" as "token map" — same thing though.

[12:22] [00:12:22] Priya: jumping to Alerts — you can create cost thresholds at route or org level; when exceeded the system creates an incident and can trigger webhooks to your pager or Slack. we also have anomaly detection for sudden per-token cost increases which often indicate prompt loop or model change.
[12:50] Michael: do alerts include sample request IDs? we need that to triage with our app logs.
[12:55] Priya: yes the alert payload includes request IDs and a stack trace of sampling points; again raw prompt text is redacted unless you opt in.

[13:30] [00:13:30] Priya: quick note on usage attribution granularity — for Hosted, attribution is per-sampled request (high fidelity), for Dedicated you get per-request exact mapping and per-pod metrics. this is useful for strict chargeback.

[14:05] [00:14:05] Priya: demoing drill into a cost spike — here's an incident from last Tuesday, the console shows the spike timeline, which route, model, and the sampled requests. you can expand the sample and see token histograms. sometimes the auto captions will combine words weirdly, e.g., "token histo gram" — it's a captioning nuisance.
[15:00] Jasmine: can these dashboards be embedded in our internal Grafana?
[15:05] Priya: yes we have a metrics export plugin and a Prometheus-compatible endpoint for per-route counters, plus a raw audit export to S3 if you want to build custom views.

[15:50] [00:15:50] Eli: network egress — for our region-specific data residency, how do you show egress costs?
[15:55] Priya: egress is tracked per-request and shown in the waterfall; if you run in a customer VPC or on-prem the egress line is zero in our hosted bill. for private deployments we provide a different billing schema and you manage intra-datacenter traffic.

[16:32] Sandra (Procurement): procurement question — what's the pricing cadence, do you bill monthly or by 30-day usage?
[16:37] Alex: monthly by usage for Hosted. for Dedicated we do committed monthly invoices and true-ups. we can include a SOW for pilot months.

[17:15] [00:17:15] Priya: quick aside — on the per-route config we also show expected latency impact if you enable batching with a 50ms hold window. in some realtime routes batching increases p95 too much so the console will warn and give a recommended hold time.

[18:00] Michael: do you surface quality regressions when applying quantization? we cannot sacrifice summary accuracy.
[18:08] Priya: yes — Optimize ties into the evals system. when you apply a quant profile we run it against your saved prompt set and show delta metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, or custom lambdas). you can set a regression alarm to block rollout.

[19:10] [00:19:10] Priya: now showing the "Compare routes" blade — here you can overlay /chat vs /summaries over time and break into cost per 1k tokens and average tokens per request. for your org we noticed /chat has a much higher tokens-per-request due to long context history.
[19:45] Jasmine: what's the best way to reduce /chat cost? reduce history size or compress context?
[19:52] Priya: both — we recommend a mix: truncate or summarize older turns server-side, enable prefix caching for static system prompts, and use cheaper embeddings for search. we can show a simulated ROI in the console.

[20:30] [00:20:30] Alex: i'll quickly flip to the billing export — you can schedule daily exports to your S3, or run ad-hoc CSVs where each row is a sampled request with route, tokens, model, cost, tenant_id. that's what we send as part of the next steps.

[21:10] [00:21:10] Jasmine: on sampling — how much sampling noise should we expect?
[21:14] Priya: sampling is default at 1% for detailed rows, but the aggregate cost numbers are derived from full telemetry so they are stable. you can increase sample rate for pilot. Dedicated gets full fidelity.

[22:05] [00:22:05] Michael: security — we need SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, RBAC mappings, and audit logs for HIPAA. can you provide those docs?
[22:18] Marcus (Redwood CSM): absolutely — we'll send SOC 2 Type II, network diagram, SAML config guide, and our HIPAA addendum. for private deployments we can do VPC peering or air-gapped installs.

[22:55] [00:22:55] Priya: one more thing — route tagging and cost centers: you can attach cost center metadata to routes and queries to slice billing by product line. customers often use this to roll up corporate chargebacks.

[23:30] Sandra: any long-term retention add-ons for audit logs and high-fidelity tokens?
[23:36] Marcus: yes — long-term retention and dedicated storage for audit trails are add-ons, and we can ship logs to your own S3 buckets for compliance.

[24:10] [00:24:10] Priya: demoing a canary change — enable prefix cache on /summaries at 5% traffic, monitor cache hit rate and quality; here you can see projected token reduction and dollar savings. at 20% hit rate you'd save roughly $2.8k/month for the route in this tenant.

[25:02] Jasmine: do you provide a change history? we need to track who toggled what.
[25:08] Priya: yes — there's an audit timeline per route showing who applied config changes, with SSO username mapping.

[26:00] [00:26:00] Priya: talking about model variants — we support on-the-fly runtime substitution: you can set a policy to use variant-A for 95% of traffic and fallback to variant-B when queue depth crosses threshold. the console simulates the hit rate and expected cost.

[26:40] Michael: curious — how do you handle fallback when the model isn't compatible (different tokenizer)?
[26:47] Priya: we only auto-fallback between compatible variants; if tokenizers differ we do a best-effort re-tokenize but we warn in the console and block the auto-fallback until an engineer approves.

[27:30] [00:27:30] Eli: operations question — what's the deployment latency for a config change? can we expect it to be near-instant?
[27:36] Priya: config changes are deployed to control plane quickly, runtime rollouts propagate in seconds to minutes depending on the scope; for Dedicated we might need a short drain window to reassign pods, usually under 2 minutes.

[28:05] [00:28:05] Alex: i want to highlight the cost-savings calculator — proj for your current traffic shows switching embeddings to a 8-bit quant profile and enabling prefix caching could reduce compute egress by ~28% while keeping p95 within target.

[28:45] Jasmine: any risk to quality with 8-bit quant?
[28:48] Priya: we run evals on your prompt set as i mentioned; if delta exceeds your threshold we don't recommend rollout. the console stores those eval results and you can download them as CSV.

[29:20] [00:29:20] Priya: moving to the "Cost anomalies" page — this has machine-detected anomalies, root cause suggestions, and quick actions like "rollback last model" or "throttle route". you can create incident playbooks that map to your oncall.

[30:00] Michael: we use PagerDuty — does that integrate?
[30:04] Priya: yes — webhook integration to PagerDuty, OpsGenie, Slack, etc.

[30:40] [00:30:40] Alex: switching to pilot specifics — recommended: spin up a Dedicated pool for /summaries (small 4-gpu pool in us-east-1) and route 20% traffic for 2 weeks to validate stability and cost. we can provide a pilot credit to reduce initial cost.

[31:12] Sandra: will procurement need a separate MSA for pilot?

[31:16] Marcus: for pilot we typically use a short SOW + pilot terms; we'll send draft MSA language.

[31:50] [00:31:50] Priya: quick Q&A from jasmine about embedding costs — the embedding route in the demo uses 4-bit quant and an approximate-nearest-neighbor cache; console shows caching hit rates and how often we call vector search versus cache.

[32:20] Jasmine: do you expose recall/precision metrics for embedding caches?
[32:24] Priya: yes, we surface retrieval metrics and let you plug in periodic evals to measure retrieval quality.

[33:00] [00:33:00] Michael: any gotchas when moving to private deployment? we have isolated network requirements and a compliance review.

[33:08] Alex: private deployments require a short on-site/remote install window; we provide an ops runbook and full checklist. network requirements are standard: NAT, specific port ranges, and optional KMS connectivity for key management. we'll attach the runbook.

[34:00] [00:34:00] Priya: demonstrating the "cost per feature" report — you can tag routes by product feature and view monthly spend per feature, helpful for PM-level reporting.

[34:31] Sandra: can we get a P0 export for finance with daily granularity for the quarter?

[34:36] Alex: yes — we'll include a daily export for the quarter in the next steps.

[35:10] [00:35:10] Priya: showing the role-based views — auditors get read-only, engineers get config rights, SREs get rollout and canary controls. SCIM maps group attrs to RBAC roles automatically.

[35:50] Michael: i want to talk about billing reconciliation — how do we reconcile if tokens reported differ from our internal counter by 0.5-1%?

[35:58] Priya: small drift can happen because tokenizers may slightly differ across runtimes; we can run a reconciliation job and provide mapping. we'll include a reconciliation table as part of the CSV export.

[36:40] [00:36:40] Jasmine: any limits on how many routes we can create? we plan many micro-routes for product lines.

[36:46] Priya: no hard limit, but for scale we recommend grouping similar endpoints or using tagging; the console scales horizontally.

[37:20] [00:37:20] Alex: quick recap: shared artifacts will be — per-route billing CSV, pilot config (Dedicated 4-gpu pool), SOC 2 + network diagram, SAML guide, draft SOW and MSA.

[37:45] Michael: that sounds good — timeline wise we want pilot started by May 20th if possible.

[37:55] Marcus: we'll aim to provision a demo tenant and have Priya seed traffic for the pilot.

[38:30] [00:38:30] Sandra: procurement question — any early termination fees for pilot?

[38:36] Alex: pilot terms are flexible, no early termination fee for the short pilot SOW. production contracts follow standard terms.

[39:10] [00:39:10] Priya: last demo clip — showing the route config JSON snippet, you can push config via the API or use the Console UI. sample curl is in the docs link i posted: https://redwood.example/decks/aurora-console-walk.pdf

[39:45] Jasmine: great, can you send that doc and the sample curl to everyone?

[39:50] Alex: yes — we'll send the deck and curl examples and the per-route export.

[40:30] [00:40:30] Michael: any mention of competitors we should be aware of? our procurement team asked whether this is comparable to OpenAI endpoints.

[40:38] Alex: folks often compare latency and cost to OpenAI; we also get questions on Anthropic and Cohere — we'll include a short doc on differences and the performance profiles.

[41:10] [00:41:10] Marcus: final notes on compliance — we'll include the HIPAA addendum and show the private deployment runbook for Aurura-ops review.

[41:45] Sandra: okay thanks everyone — next steps and action items?

[41:50] Alex: recap of next steps: we'll email the CSV and pilot config, send SOC2 + SAML guide, draft SOW. action items assigned in the chat.

[42:20] [00:42:20] Michael: thanks — appreciate the thorough run-through.
[42:25] Jasmine: thanks all, that was helpful.
[42:30] [00:42:30] Meeting end.
